mode: 'you' right after 'Could' or 'Can' opening a user's request to the assistant
'and' or 'She' after a character smiles or nods in a children's story
colon after 'assistant' starting a reply, mostly 'Sure' after a user request
colon after 'user' or 'assistant' role label in chat transcripts; also a citation digit

summary: Fires on chat-transcript structure ('you' after Could/Can, colons after role labels) and story narration; not emotion-related.

mode: 'a', 'her', 'his' after 'had', 'with', 'asked' in a child's story about possessions
period ending a child's sentence about an outing or plan (park, lake, candy store)
'and' right after 'smiled' or 'laughed' in children's stories
character name or pronoun opening a sentence after another character's problem (Billy, Max, He)
function words in simple stories: 'with' before 'their hands', 'I' in 'Can I push'

summary: Fires on function words and subject references in simple children's stories, predicting the next action; not emotion-related.

mode: clause-final word in children's stories: 'water', 'fast', 'quiet', 'feeling', 'and'
period or 'position' ending an exercise instruction step (plank, child's pose, shrug)
'background' before '-color' in CSS hover and nth-child rules

summary: Fires on clause-final words in children's stories, exercise instructions and CSS 'background-color'; not emotion-related.

mode: 'next' in 'next week' or 'next time' after a future event (presentation, big test)
'over' in 'over the last year' or 'over the past 30 years' in news and reports
'time' in 'had such a great time', 'facing', 'well', 'there' closing a clause
'years' in time spans: 'two years ago', 'a year ago', '15 to 20 years from now'
'unable' in assistant refusals, 'the' before 'article', 'consistent' in a science paper

summary: Fires on time-span and clause-ending words in news, stories and chat; mainly temporal phrasing, not emotion-related.

mode: verb or complement after 'happy that she', 'brave enough to', 'had found' in children's stories
'Thank' opening 'Thank you' gratitude in children's dialogue
'than' in 'more toys than you', 'To' in 'What To Do', 'a' in 'There are a variety'

summary: Fires on verbs and 'Thank' openers in children's stories and a few comparison or recipe phrases; not emotion-related.

mode: 'so' or 'very' right before a feeling or pretty adjective: 'was so proud', 'were so happy', 'was very sad'
't' or 'not' in 'didn't know' or 'did not want' while a character is scared or tense
'wanted' after a character's fear or frustration: 'Jane wanted to escape', 'wanted to cry'
'She' or 'He' starting a sentence right after an excited, amazed or proud sentence
'to' after 'started' before cry, frown, walk or feel tired
'scared' (also 'sad') right after 'was', describing a character's feeling
opening quote mark starting dialogue after narration, e.g. 'Hi Timmy!' or 'Oh Sweetie'
period right after feeling words: 'feeling guilty and sad.', 'feeling very scared.', 'felt happy.'
digits, periods or 'Jul' inside bibliography and citation text
'.' after 'said Sarah excitedly', 'It' after a soft noise, 'were' in 'They were playing jazz'

summary: Fires on intensifiers, negations and story tokens; several modes sit on fear, sadness or pride words, but it also covers citations, so it is only partly emotion-related.

mode: 'he', 'were', 'atmosphere', 'opinion', 'And' in essays on people's temperament and opinions
period ending a sentence in essays or news about parties, climate, or markets
mixed: ')' in a title citation, 'and' in a building description, 'the' before 'main gateway'

summary: Fires on sentence boundaries and function words in history, news and essay text; no feeling link.

mode: 'a', 'some', 'for' before a flavour adjective in baked potato recipe toppings
'exposure', 'reach', 'faced', 'social' in child-education and programme text
'knew' or 'told' right after a character's kind or happy action: 'Max knew', 'Lily knew'
'proud' right after 'felt', 'was so', 'were very' describing a character
adjective after 'a' or 'was' describing an object: thick, heavy, small, silver, soft
'still' after 'you can', 'secured' in news, 'keep' in 'to keep the story engaging'

summary: Fires on modifier and verb tokens across lists, news and stories; only the 'proud' mode is clearly emotion-related.
